This development study asks where a distribution test complements conventional
mean differential expression. It reuses 240 frozen count matrices and their
native DESeq2/edgeR fits, and recomputes WADE with the production API. There is
no assumed crossover and no conclusion is based solely on a favorable example.

The count generator is a documented WADE pattern extension using empirical
mean/dispersion pairs from compcodeR; it is **not an unmodified published
benchmark**. The [reference notebook](reference-benchmarks.qmd) adds unmodified
compcodeR, airway, Schurch yeast and original OUTRIDER backgrounds. The frozen
[source protocol](../archive/development-20260923/docs/large-cohort-development.md) documents all patterns,
seeds and native settings.

Read calibration before sensitivity. All inputs, native fits and current
results—including unfavorable outcomes—are retained with checksums. Formal
equivalence, clinical rarity detection and broad sparse-assay calibration are
not established here. Results and figures await approval.

## Design and endpoints

There are 2,000 measured genes and 20 independent matrices per geometry/panel.
The balanced series uses 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 250 and 500 samples per group;
a separate series holds controls at 50 (100, 250 and 500 cases). Complete-null
matrices are tested at 50:50 and 500:500. Initial pooled total-count eligibility
and the native RLE reference are preserved, with factor parity checked.
WADE's refresh uses a prespecified 49,999 cap, seed 20260919 and q=0.05.
This cap supports an isolated 5% discovery in the 2,000-gene family; it does
not make floor p-values precise. The production default uses a larger cap.

Recovery below means the fraction of truly altered genes called, retaining
filtered alternatives in the denominator. Pure shape changes differ from the
mean-DE hypothesis, so recovery is coverage of a shared biological alteration
set, not a claim that all methods test identical nulls. Calibration exports
include both the distribution-null FDP and each method's own target-null FDP.
Native defaults, including DESeq2 filtering and Cook's behavior, are preserved;
the no-Cook's sensitivity arm is explicitly identified.

## The normalization limit

At 500:500, WADE recovers 75.8% of altered genes, versus 60.6% for default
DESeq2. But their mean distribution-null FDPs are 20.0% and 23.8%, respectively.
Those recovery figures do **not** demonstrate a calibrated win.

A post-refresh diagnostic reruns the same 20 difficult matrices with their
known generating exposures, preserving the test, filtering, seed and budget.
WADE's mean FDP falls to 3.46% (replicate-level 95% interval 2.98–3.94%),
with 71.3% recovery. This isolates a substantial normalization contribution in
this setting. Known exposures are an oracle diagnostic, not a factor estimator
available to an analyst; these reused matrices are not fresh confirmation.

```{python}
#| label: known-exposure-diagnostic
#| output: asis
diagnostic,diagnostic_source=CS.load(ROOT,"reference-diagnostic",OUT,table="metrics.tsv")
fdp=CS.summary(diagnostic,["method"],"fdp")
power=CS.summary(diagnostic,["method"],"power")
export_table(CS.as_polars(fdp),OUT,"known-exposure-fdp")
export_table(CS.as_polars(power),OUT,"known-exposure-power")
def interval(row):
    return f"{100*row['mean']:.2f}% [{100*row.lo:.2f}, {100*row.hi:.2f}]"
joined=fdp[["method"]].copy()
joined["Mean FDP (95% interval)"]=fdp.apply(interval,axis=1)
joined["Recovery (95% interval)"]=power.apply(interval,axis=1)
table(joined,"known-exposure-display",{"method":"Reference"})
```

A majority of unchanged genes does not guarantee negligible reference bias
at large n. Validated controls or external exposures can help; this diagnostic
does not certify an automatic selector.

## Limited controls and fixed event counts

Adding cases is not equivalent to adding control information. With a fixed
number of affected cases, a larger cohort also dilutes prevalence. These
contrasts are retained even where WADE has little power.

```{python}
#| label: fig-limited-controls
#| fig-cap: "The case-size series with 50 controls. A larger case cohort alone does not guarantee tail sensitivity."
fig,imbalanced=CS.power_grid(scores,categories,geometry="fixed_control")
export_table(CS.as_polars(imbalanced),OUT,"limited-control-summary")
fig
```

```{python}
#| label: fixed-event-table
#| output: asis
fixed=scores[(scores.panel=="mixed") & (scores.geometry=="balanced") & scores.category.str.startswith("fixed_k")]
fixed=CS.summary(fixed,["method","category","n_case"],"power")
export_table(CS.as_polars(fixed),OUT,"fixed-event-summary")
fixed["Affected cases"]=fixed.category.str.extract(r"affected(\d+)").astype(int)
display=fixed[fixed.n_case.isin([50,500])].pivot(index=["n_case","Affected cases"],columns="method",values="mean").reset_index()
table(display[["n_case","Affected cases","WADE","DESeq2","DESeq2-no-Cooks","edgeR-QL"]],"fixed-event-display",
    {"n_case":"Samples/group","DESeq2-no-Cooks":"DESeq2†","edgeR-QL":"edgeR"})
```

The table reports mean recovery; complete replicate intervals remain in the
exports. † DESeq2 with Cook’s exclusion disabled, a labeled sensitivity arm.
